prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands at magic twist angles in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, opening the field of moire quantum materials

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a concrete, teachable discovery with a clean theory-plus-experiment structure: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands in 2011, and Jarillo-Herrero's group found correlated insulators and superconductivity in 2018. Within a few years it was reproduced by many groups and spread to a large family of moire systems with tunable interactions. It is also the candidate that most colleagues ranked highly (all eight members place it in their top eight, four of them in the top three), so it has the broadest cross-subfield support on the table. It fits the criterion that the prize is for a discovery or invention with identifiable people behind it, and the three supplied names map onto prediction and observation. I ranked it second in my opening view; after reading colleagues I now put it first.
statement.case_against: The field is under a decade old and the pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is still unsettled, so a prize could be judged early. Device-to-device variation from twist-angle disorder and strain also means the phase diagram is not fully universal. Attribution is imperfect: Cao and the experimental team, and other groups such as Dean's with hBN heterostructures, are outside the credited names, and the Nobel rules limit us to three. A committee that values long stability of interpretation could reasonably prefer Kane-Molenkamp (B031) or the clocks (B022) this year.

responses.point: Kroll puts optical lattice clocks (B022) first as a direct realisation of measurement-driven progress, with Katori and Ye as a fair two-person prize, and he regards moire graphene as arguably somewhat early.
responses.response: I agree that B022 is the cleaner attribution and the more mature result, and I keep it as an alternative. I disagree on timing for B028: the existence of the flat-band correlated phases has been independently confirmed by many groups, and what is unsettled is the interpretation of the superconductivity, not the discovery. Our question is whether a discovery is secure, not whether every mechanism is closed. The clock prize also overlaps with the 2005 and 2012 frequency-metrology awards, which he acknowledges, whereas B028 opens a new platform.

responses.point: Johansson ranks circuit QED (B014) first and B028 third, finding the idea simple and original but noting that the interpretation of the superconductivity is not settled and recognition would be somewhat early.
responses.response: I share his reservation on the interpretation but weigh it differently. His own case for B014 stresses that a prize so soon after the 2025 superconducting-circuit award could be too close, and I think that concern is real. B028 does not have that problem. I would also ask him whether the unsettled mechanism is a reason to wait when we gave prizes for the fractional quantum Hall effect and for topological phases while their interpretation was still being refined. The decisive point for me is that the discovery rests on reproducible measurements. As a microscopist I would add that twist-angle inhomogeneity is now directly mapped in real devices, which narrows that uncertainty.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks DMFT (B018) first and B028 second, seeing a clean theory-plus-experiment pairing with broad impact, but noting that the experiments involved a larger team and other groups reproduced them.
responses.response: I agree with his reading of the pairing and with the allocation concern about Cao and co-workers; a three-name limit forces an omission, and I would not pretend otherwise. We differ on B018: DMFT is a method with an overdue case, but its attribution between the infinite-dimension limit and the impurity-model mapping is harder to settle from the supplied names than the B028 split between prediction and observation. I could support DMFT as an alternative if the committee wants a theory prize, but I do not have it among my top choices because the discovery is less sharply dated.

responses.point: Pearce ranks IceCube (B002, Halzen alone) first and Kane with Molenkamp third, and proposes only Kane and Molenkamp as the cleanest pairing from B031, leaving Mele and the BHZ theorists unresolved.
responses.response: On B031 I agree the credit problem is real and that Mele and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang cannot be added from this entry. I included Xue in my opening trio for the quantum anomalous Hall observation, but I now accept his point that this is a distinct sub-discovery, so I would not extend a topological prize to a third strand. On B002 I share his hesitation about a single laureate for a collaboration that large, and I would want the committee to say clearly why Halzen alone captures the decisive role before I support it.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks the Higgs discovery (B037) first as a first-rank experimental achievement that complements the 2013 theory prize, while admitting the detector trio is a simplification of a thousands-strong collaboration.
responses.response: I do not dispute the importance or maturity of the discovery, and I ranked B037 seventh because it matters. My reservation is about attribution, not merit: crediting three founding leaders of ATLAS and CMS over the people who built the detectors and led the 2012 analyses is a principle we would have to argue and defend. I would want that argument made explicitly. Compared with that, B028 has an identifiable, small set of people whose papers carry the result.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges a field under a decade old, with the superconducting pairing mechanism unresolved, to be mature enough.
Whether Bistritzer should share the theory credit with MacDonald, and how to treat Cao and the experimental team under the three-person limit.
Whether Kane and Molenkamp (B031) without Mele, Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang could be defended as a fair allocation.
Whether the committee will want to avoid a second condensed-matter materials prize in a year when atomic or particle physics candidates are also strong.
statement.conflict_note: My profile shows no specific connection to the B028 candidates. For B001 (my own opening first choice) I work on LaAlO3/SrTiO3 oxide interfaces and oxygen vacancies by transmission electron microscopy, so I judge that candidate from close scientific involvement and would be cautious about advocating it too strongly; it has little support from colleagues and I have not made it my preferred configuration. Göran Johansson is also at Chalmers, which is a documented institutional connection, though I see no shared project with the shortlisted candidates.
